title: Dedicated Console UI: show tier, committed throughput, utilization, and throughput SLO status
creator: Lauren Bishop
content:
## Context
Dedicated is getting formal tiering (Standard/Plus/Premium) + a throughput SLO. We need to expose the tier, the committed throughput floor, current utilization (incl. burst), and “SLO status” in Console so customers and CS can self-serve answers.

This ticket covers the UX/design spec for the initial in-console surfaces. Engineering implementation will be tracked separately.

## Goals
1) Make it obvious (no support ticket required) what a customer bought:
- Tier (Standard / Plus / Premium)
- Region + hardware shape
- Committed throughput floor (tokens/sec) and how it’s measured
- Whether burst is enabled and how much has been consumed (where applicable)

2) Provide a clear “are we meeting the guarantee?” signal:
- Current SLO status (Good / At risk / Breached)
- Recent compliance window (rolling) and link to details
- Explicit exclusions caveat (e.g., customer throttling / unsupported model versions)

3) Reduce back-and-forth during escalations:
- Give CS/Solutions an at-a-glance view and a consistent set of numbers to reference
- Link to internal dashboards/runbooks (internal-only)

## Non-goals (v1)
- Full contract/SLA text in Console
- A customer-facing incident timeline (we can link to Status page externally; internal incident tooling is separate)
- Per-route deep breakdowns (we’ll show deployment-level first; add drilldowns later)

## Proposed information architecture
### Surface A: Dedicated Deployment Overview (customer-facing)
Placement: Deployment details page header area + “Dedicated” section within Overview.

Components:
1) **Tier + Shape summary pill**
- Copy: “Dedicated • Plus” (tier) + “us-east • shape: h100x8”
- Tooltip: quick tier definition + link to docs

2) **Committed throughput card**
- Primary metric: “Committed throughput floor”
- Value: e.g., “85k tok/s” (deployment-level; aggregated across replicas)
- Secondary text: “Measured as p50 sustained output tokens/sec over 5-min windows. Exclusions apply.”
- Link: “How this is calculated” (opens modal)

3) **Utilization card (now)**
- Primary metric: “Current throughput” (live-ish: last 5 min)
- Secondary: “% of committed” + small sparkline (last 60 min)
- If burst enabled: show “Burst: On” + “Burst used (24h): X tok/s-min equivalents” (final unit TBD by metering; use text label until unit is stable)
- If throttled/admission-controlled: show banner “Requests are being rate-limited to protect guarantees” with link to guidance

4) **Throughput SLO status widget (summary)**
- Status chip: Good / At risk / Breached
- Short explanation based on most recent evaluation window
- Link: “View details” to Surface B

### Surface B: Dedicated → SLO Status page (customer-facing)
A dedicated sub-page or tab for “SLO status”.

Sections:
1) **Status summary**
- “Current status” + last evaluated window timestamp
- “SLO target” (e.g., “Committed floor met in 99.5% of 5-min windows over 28 days”) — confirm exact phrasing with SRE/Legal

2) **Compliance chart**
- Time series of “observed throughput (p50)” vs “committed floor”
- Default range: 7 days; switcher: 24h / 7d / 28d
- Visual: floor as a horizontal line, observed as line/area; highlight windows below floor

3) **Recent breaches (if any)**
- Table: start/end, duration, min observed throughput, remediation note (customer-friendly)
- If no breaches: empty state “No breaches in selected range.”

4) **Exclusions & measurement (collapsible)**
- Bullet list of common exclusions (high-level)
- “What counts as throughput” definition (output tokens/sec; streaming handled consistently)
- Note: “If your model/version differs from the pinned deployment config, results may vary.”

### Surface C (internal-only): CS/Support view
This is a permissioned variant of the same pages (Redwood staff only) with additional links:
- “Open internal dashboard” (Grafana/Observability pack)
- “Runbook: Dedicated throughput SLO escalation”
- “Pager policy / oncall rotation”

Implementation note: if staff-vs-customer mode is hard, we can put internal links behind a feature flag or hide behind RBAC.

## Data requirements / sources (alignment targets)
- Tier + entitlements: control plane config / billing plan metadata (PM to confirm canonical source)
- Committed throughput: configuration field on deployment (committed_tok_s)
- Observed throughput: canonical per-deployment throughput metric (ENG-19244)
- SLO status: evaluator output / SLO toolkit summary (ENG-19288)
- Burst usage: metering events (ENG-19302)

## Copy guidelines (draft)
- Prefer “Committed throughput floor” over “Guaranteed” in UI. Use “guarantee” only in docs/contract context.
- Use “tokens/sec (tok/s)” consistently; avoid mixing with requests/sec.
- Always include “How it’s measured” affordance next to committed throughput.

Example strings:
- “Committed throughput floor: 85k tok/s”
- Tooltip: “Your Dedicated deployment is provisioned to sustain at least 85k output tokens/sec under supported conditions. See measurement details.”
- SLO status (good): “Meeting committed throughput in the current evaluation window.”
- SLO status (at risk): “Throughput is trending near the committed floor. If sustained, this may count against the SLO.”
- SLO status (breached): “Committed throughput was not met for some windows in the selected range.”

## Edge cases / design notes
- Multi-model deployments: show committed throughput at deployment-level; in v1 we do not split by model. Add note in measurement modal: “If multiple models are configured, throughput is measured at the deployment boundary.”
- Warm-up / newly provisioned deployments: SLO status widget should show “Collecting data” until minimum window is available (e.g., first 60 minutes) with explanation.
- Customer-side throttling: if we can detect client rate limits / 429s, show a callout “Client requests are being throttled; this can affect observed throughput.” (PM/SRE to confirm whether this should be shown externally.)
- Streaming: ensure observed throughput uses corrected accounting (see PR-19422); avoid showing inconsistent “live” numbers vs SLO evaluator numbers.

## Acceptance criteria
- Dedicated deployment page shows tier and committed throughput floor in a single place that Sales/CS can screenshot.
- Customers can view a single “SLO status” value + click through to see compliance over 7/28 days.
- Exclusions/measurement are accessible inline (modal or collapsible) without leaving Console.
- Internal mode provides direct links to dashboards + runbook.

## Design deliverables
- Figma frames:
  - Dedicated deployment overview (header + cards)
  - SLO status page (summary + chart + recent breaches)
  - Measurement details modal
  - Internal-only link section
- Redlines / component specs for:
  - Status chip states (Good/At risk/Breached/Collecting)
  - Chart annotations and empty states

## Links
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/dedicated-throughput-slo-prd.json
- Dashboard spec: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/dedicated-throughput-slo-dashboards.json
- SLO definition: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/dedicated-throughput-slo-definition.json
- Related design: DES-784 (throughput SLO status widget exploration)
- Eng dependencies: ENG-19244 (per-deployment throughput metrics), ENG-19288 (burn-rate alerts), ENG-19302 (burst metering)

## Updates / comments
### 2025-02-19 (Lauren Bishop)
Adding this after multiple enterprise calls asked “where can we see what you’re committing to?” We need something in Console before tier GA.

### 2025-02-24 (Sergio Costa)
From observability side: we can provide a summarized SLO evaluator output (status + window compliance) as a lightweight API for Console. Recommend Console displays the evaluator’s result rather than re-deriving from raw metrics to avoid drift.

### 2025-02-27 (Sean Gallagher)
Design note: please avoid wording that implies instantaneous guarantees. The SLO is windowed. We should always pair committed floor with the measurement window definition.

### 2025-03-04 (Rafael Mendes)
For “At risk”, prefer deterministic logic (e.g., burn rate > threshold) rather than heuristics. UI should be able to map evaluator states 1:1.

### 2025-03-10 (Allison Grant)
Please keep the main deployment page simple: 3-4 key metrics max, everything else behind a details click. Customers will compare across vendors; clarity matters.

### 2025-03-18 (Lauren Bishop)
Aligned with Legal: UI can say “Committed throughput floor” and “SLO status” but should not show contractual remedy language (credits) in v1.

### 2025-03-21 (Lauren Bishop)
Marking Done for design scope: consolidated spec written, widget exploration split to DES-784. Next step is eng kickoff with Console + telemetry owners and confirm exact metric labels/units once ENG-19302 lands.
